newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PILTEL H1 NET SHARPLY LOWER, H2 SEEN BETTER.
newsitem.headline: PILTEL H1 NET SHARPLY LOWER, H2 SEEN BETTER.

text.p: Fraudulent calls marred earnings of mobile phone firm Pilipino Telephone Co (Piltel) so much that on Friday when it reported a 66 percent drop in profits for the first half of the year, analysts still said it was better than expected.
Piltel said its profits fell to 165.8 million in the first six months of the year compared to 487.6 million in the same period last year.

"It's more than what we were expecting but still bad compared to last year," said Gina Roa-Dipaling, analyst at Paribas Asia Equity who expects the company to generate close to 400 million profits this year.
Dipaling said she had twice downgraded earnings forecast for the company, first, after the release of first quarter earnings and second, after the peso's de facto devaluation last month.

"My expectation was 270 million pesos for the full year and they may even exceed it with the first half results," said Anscor-Hagedorn Securities analyst Russell Ong who downscaled his full-year one billion peso net income forecast last April.

The cellular phone firm said its operating expenses for the first six months soared largely due to a 327 percent rise in its provision for doubtful accounts at 254.3 million pesos from 59.6 million a year ago.
Piltel suffered massive cloning problems last year, causing the firm to allocate 886.35 million pesos for doubtful accounts.
Since then, the firm has installed several anti-fraud measures to prevent fraud calls.

"Piltel is kept hostage by cloning racketeers. It's hard to implement the anti-cloning measures and achieve a 100 percent success rate at once," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
Despite the cloning problems, Piltel said its subscribers as of end-June rose to 349,000 compared to 281,000 a year ago.

"I think the second half will be better than the first when they were focusing on the review of their operations to help stem the cloning problem. With the anti-fraud measures in place, they can now step up marketing measures," said Sun Hung Kai Securities vice-president for research Raul Ruiz.
Ruiz earlier projected over one billion peso full year earnings and downscaled it to 500 million last April.
"There will be some sort of improvement for the second half as a result of the house cleaning measures," said Dipaling.

Guoco's Mejia said the entry of APC Group Inc will help provide Piltel with additional liquidity. Philippine Global Communications (Philcom), a unit of APC, recently bought more than 20 percent stake in Piltel.
Analysts said despite a likely improvement in second half earnings, full-year net income will be lower than 1996.
In 1996, Piltel posted a 710.47 million in net profits.
The de facto devaluation will also cast a pall on Piltel's earnings for the full year, analysts added.
Ruiz said the peso's depreciation will translate to a six percent reduction in his full-year profits forecast assuming the peso will settle at 28 to the dollar.
